column2: Trumpeter and bandleader who repeatedly reshaped modern jazz, from cool and hard bop to modal jazz and electric fusion. Start with Kind of Blue.
Tenor and soprano saxophonist who moved from hard bop through complex harmonic cycles to extended modal and spiritual improvisation. Hear Giant Steps and A Love Supreme.
New Orleans trumpeter and singer whose strong solo voice transformed early ensemble jazz. His phrasing, swing and scat singing influenced generations.
Composer, pianist and bandleader who wrote for the distinctive voices of his orchestra. His work spans intricate big-band portraits, suites and songs.
Jazz vocalist celebrated for precise pitch, lively scat improvisations and wide-ranging Song Book recordings of American standards.
Singer whose flexible timing and intimate tone made familiar melodies sound deeply personal. Lady in Satin and earlier small-group sides show different eras.
Alto saxophonist whose fluid, harmonically daring lines helped define bebop. His improvisations recast the blues and the changes of popular songs.
Virtuoso trumpeter, composer and bandleader central to bebop and Afro-Cuban jazz; famed for angular lines, rhythmic play and work with Chano Pozo.
Pianist and composer known for spare, angular melodies, distinctive dissonance and unexpected silence. Wrote Round Midnight, Blue Monk and Straight, No Chaser.
Pianist who brought luminous voicings and close bass-drum interaction to the jazz trio. Hear the Village Vanguard recordings and Waltz for Debby.
Driving drummer and leader of the Jazz Messengers, a hard-bop school for generations of improvisers. His press-roll accents and ensemble energy are unmistakable.
Bassist, composer and bandleader whose works blend blues, gospel, counterpoint and collective improvisation. His groups often balance tightly written music with raw freedom.
Alto saxophonist with a rich blues-inflected sound who bridged hard bop, soul jazz and modal playing; heard with Miles Davis and his own quintet.
Trumpeter and vocalist associated with West Coast cool jazz; known for a lyrical, restrained tone and intimate singing as well as turbulent personal history.
Tenor saxophonist celebrated for thematic improvisation, rhythmic wit and unaccompanied cadenzas. Saxophone Colossus showcases his musical storytelling.
Pianist whose fleet single-note right-hand lines and modern left-hand comping helped establish the language of bebop piano.
Pianist and composer who mixed blues, gospel and strong rhythmic hooks into hard bop; his memorable compositions include Song for My Father.
Saxophonist and composer whose enigmatic melodies shaped the Jazz Messengers, Miles Davis's quintet and Weather Report.
Pianist and composer equally at home in post-bop harmony, electronic jazz and funk. His work ranges from Maiden Voyage to Head Hunters.
Pianist and composer who explored acoustic trio jazz, Latin rhythms and electric fusion, including Return to Forever.
Guitarist and composer recognized for lyrical melodies, spacious ensemble textures and a long-running group with keyboardist Lyle Mays.
Guitarist whose warm thumb-picked tone, octave melodies and chord solos became hallmarks of modern jazz guitar.
Pianist and vocalist who drew on classical training, blues, jazz, gospel and protest song to build an expressive, genre-defying repertoire.
Trumpeter with a brilliant tone and agile hard-bop lines; a vital voice on sessions led by Art Blakey, Herbie Hancock and others.
Tenor saxophonist and composer with an earthy sound and intricate rhythmic phrasing. His recordings range from hard bop to modal exploration.
Trumpeter of exuberant hard-bop lines and punchy melodies; his composition The Sidewinder helped bring soul jazz to a wider audience.
Pianist whose powerful left hand, quartal voicings and modal drive formed a signature part of John Coltrane's classic quartet.
Adventurous improviser on alto saxophone, bass clarinet and flute whose angular phrases expanded jazz's sonic vocabulary.
Alto saxophonist and composer whose melodically driven free-jazz approach challenged conventional chord progressions and solo roles.
Tenor saxophonist associated with spiritual jazz; combined fierce overblowing, long modal vamps and searching, vocal-like phrases.
Clarinetist and bandleader central to the swing era; led celebrated big bands and small groups and played at Carnegie Hall in 1938.
Pianist and bandleader whose spare keyboard style, riff arrangements and buoyant rhythm section made Kansas City swing a defining sound.
Pianist and bandleader whose quartet explored unusual meters and clear melodic contrasts; Time Out includes Paul Desmond's Take Five.
Baritone saxophonist and arranger associated with cool jazz; known for an airy pianoless quartet featuring trumpet and baritone sax.
Tenor saxophonist admired for a smooth lyrical sound, from cool jazz to Brazilian bossa nova collaborations with Joao Gilberto.
Canadian pianist with prodigious technique, a strong swing pulse and rich blues vocabulary; a major trio leader and accompanist.
Singer renowned for an operatic vocal range, sophisticated harmony and flexible phrasing across ballads and up-tempo jazz.
Singer known as the Queen of the Blues who moved fluently among jazz, blues and rhythm-and-blues with clear diction and emotional control.
Pianist whose early trio style helped shape intimate small-combo jazz; later became a hugely successful singer of popular standards.
Stride pianist, organist, composer and entertainer whose infectious swing and virtuosic left hand made him a Harlem jazz original.
Pianist, composer and arranger whose career linked swing, bebop and later modern jazz; she mentored younger improvisers.
Pianist and composer whose idiosyncratic post-bop harmony and open forms are heard on Point of Departure.
Hard-bop pianist and composer whose gospel-rooted grooves helped shape the sound of Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers.
Trumpeter whose clear articulation, lyrical phrasing and brilliant technique influenced hard bop despite his brief career.
Tenor saxophonist with a broad tone and unhurried, behind-the-beat phrasing; a key bridge between swing and bebop.
Pianist famed for exceptional virtuosity, harmonic substitutions and dazzling reworkings of popular-song melodies.
Tenor saxophonist whose raw timbre, marching-song motifs and intense improvisations made him a distinctive free-jazz voice.
Pianist, composer and bandleader who united large-ensemble jazz, electronic textures and Afrofuturist performance art in his Arkestra.
Composer and saxophonist whose experimental music crosses avant-garde jazz, improvisation, film scores and klezmer influences.
Pianist known for extended solo improvisations, the Standards Trio and an intensely spontaneous approach to melody and harmony.
Pianist whose trio playing combines contrapuntal clarity, shifting meters and reinterpretations of rock and pop repertoire.
Austrian keyboardist and composer who shaped electric jazz in Miles Davis's groups and co-founded Weather Report.
Electric bassist whose fretless tone, harmonics and melodic virtuosity broadened the role of bass in jazz fusion.
Drummer whose explosive polyrhythms reshaped Miles Davis's 1960s quintet and helped drive early electric fusion.
Drummer and composer who helped create bebop's modern rhythmic vocabulary and later connected jazz with civil-rights themes.
Drummer whose ride-cymbal pulse and displaced bass/snare accents helped establish modern bebop drumming.
Double bassist best known for supple walking lines and melodic solos in Miles Davis's 1950s groups and many hard-bop recordings.
Bassist and cellist whose elastic time and harmonic imagination shaped Miles Davis's 1960s quintet and thousands of recordings.
Hammond organist whose bluesy phrasing and bass-pedal grooves made the organ trio a major soul-jazz format.
Belgian-born Romani guitarist whose dazzling improvisation and partnership with violinist Stephane Grappelli helped establish gypsy jazz.
West Coast alto saxophonist whose lyrical yet urgent playing mixes cool-jazz clarity with bebop and blues inflection.
Trumpeter and educator whose virtuosity, traditional jazz advocacy and leadership at Jazz at Lincoln Center influenced modern jazz institutions.
Pianist, harpist and composer whose spiritual-jazz recordings combine modal improvisation with strings, organ and meditative textures.
